reference: GNU coreutils basename, invoked by system Bash with the harness reference PATH, is the independent oracle for runnable cases. The loadable's one-string/optional-suffix behavior follows its documented POSIX-style basename contract; the metadata case is based on the embedded basename_doc and Bash type/help builtins.
coverage: Bash builtin registration and documented help metadata
ordinary path component extraction and single-component names
leading-dash operands after the option terminator
empty input and invalid operand counts
exclusions: GNU-only multi-name, NUL-output, and option-driven modes are outside the stock Bash loadable's documented string [suffix] interface.
The operation has no filesystem or privileged side effects, so no VM or syscall-mock case is needed.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash exposes basename as a builtin and its help includes the synopsis documented in the loadable source.
cases.script: [[ $(type -t basename) == builtin ]]; help_text=$(help basename); [[ $help_text == *"Return non-directory portion of pathname."* ]]; [[ $help_text == *"pathname component in STRING."* ]]; printf 'builtin; basename help matches documented synopsis\n'
cases.stdout: builtin; basename help matches documented synopsis

cases.purpose: Extract the final component from a multi-component path, a single-component name, and a path ending in a component without a suffix.
Check removal of repeated trailing slashes and the special result for an operand made only of slash characters.
Check stripping of a matching suffix, retention of a nonmatching suffix, and retention when the suffix equals the entire basename.
Use GNU's option terminator to pass a leading-dash name as an operand, both alone and after a directory prefix.
Preserve spaces in an operand and leave a leading-dot filename intact when no matching suffix is present.
Check the empty-string boundary separately from a slash-only operand, whose specified result is a single slash.
Check GNU's failure status and diagnostic policy when the required name operand is omitted.
Check rejection of more than the documented name and optional suffix operands.
